title: PSAT Practice Test: Free Resources & Strategies
summary: The best free PSAT practice tests come from College Board and Acely. Find Bluebook, Acely's 10 adaptive tests, and how to get more from each one.
body_markdown:
The best free PSAT practice tests come from College Board and Acely. College Board's Bluebook app has full-length, adaptive PSAT/NMSQT and PSAT 10 practice tests that match test day. Acely's 3-day free trial includes 10 more adaptive PSAT practice tests with score reports, pacing insights, and an AI tutor. Below: where to find them, how to space them out, and what to do after the PSAT.


## Where to find free PSAT practice tests


- **Bluebook (official, digital, adaptive).** Full-length practice tests in the same app you'll use on test day. Under Practice and Prepare, choose Full-Length Practice, set Test Type to PSAT-Related Assessments, then pick PSAT 8/9 or PSAT/NMSQT and PSAT 10. College Board offers 3 of each.[Download Bluebook](https://bluebook.collegeboard.org/) .
- **[Acely (10 adaptive PSAT tests)](https://acely.com/psat-prep) .** Get 10 full-length PSAT practice tests with score reports, pacing insights and an AI tutor to target your areas of improvement.


College Board says PSAT/NMSQT and PSAT 10 practice materials can be used interchangeably, so a PSAT 10 practice test works for PSAT/NMSQT prep too.


## Get ready for the PSAT


PSAT prep builds familiarity with SAT-style questions and can help with scholarship eligibility. Full-length practice tests matter most here. They're how you learn the timing, the adaptive format, and Bluebook's tools before test day.


### PSAT format at a glance


Reading and Writing Math


Questions 54 (2 modules of 27) 44 (2 modules of 22)


Time 64 minutes (32 per module) 70 minutes (35 per module)


Section score 160–760 160–760


Calculator N/A Desmos graphing calculator on every question


Total: 98 questions in 2 hours and 14 minutes, scored from 320–1520.


The PSAT is adaptive. Module 1 in each section is the same for everyone. Your Module 1 score decides whether Module 2 is easier or harder. A full-length practice test captures that better than a worksheet of random questions. For scoring details, see our[PSAT score guide](https://acely.com/psat-prep/psat-score-guide) .


## Why the PSAT matters


The PSAT/NMSQT prepares you for SAT content and timing, and your score report highlights skills to work on before the SAT. If you take it in 11th grade, it's also the qualifying test for the National Merit Scholarship Program, based on your Selection Index and your state's cutoff. Our[National Merit Scholarship guide](https://acely.com/psat-prep/national-merit-scholarship-guide) covers how that works.


## Use full-length practice tests


Full-length tests help with:


- pacing control
- test-day stamina
- Bluebook tools like the built-in Desmos calculator, highlighter, and flag-for-review
- timed conditions


Short practice sets are useful for skill work. A full test is what shows how you hold up across 2 hours and 14 minutes.


## Practice with Bluebook


To take an official PSAT practice test:


1. [Download Bluebook](https://bluebook.collegeboard.org/) on the computer or tablet you'll test with
2. Go to Practice and Prepare
3. Choose Full-Length Practice
4. Under Test Type, select PSAT-Related Assessments
5. Under Test, select PSAT 8/9 or PSAT/NMSQT and PSAT 10
6. Take one test as a baseline and save another to measure progress later


Bluebook practice tests are timed like the real test and scored when you finish. Results show up in My Practice. If you test with accommodations, you can select them when you set up the test and see how they'll work on test day.


## Other free PSAT resources


- **[PSAT/NMSQT Student Guide](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/psat-nmsqt-student-guide.pdf) :** College Board's overview of the test, test-day rules, and sample questions.
- **[Khan Academy](https://www.khanacademy.org/test-prep/sat) :** free lessons and practice by skill, built with College Board. Useful for filling content gaps between full-length tests.
- **[Student Question Bank](https://satsuitequestionbank.collegeboard.org/) :** official questions you can filter by skill and difficulty. Good for drilling one weak area at a time.
- **[SAT Question of the Day](https://qotd.collegeboard.org/) :** one official question a day. A simple habit for the weeks before your test.

## How to space out your practice tests


How many tests you take depends on how much time you have before test day.


- **1 week or less:** Take 1 full-length official test in Bluebook under real timing. Spend the rest of your time reviewing every missed question.
- **About 1 month:** Take an official test as your baseline, practice your weakest skills for 2–3 weeks, then take a second full test about a week before the PSAT. Our[1-month PSAT study plan](https://acely.com/psat-prep/1-month-psat-study-plan) lays out each week.
- **2–3 months:** Start with an official baseline, then alternate a full-length test every 2–3 weeks with targeted skill practice in between. Save one official Bluebook test for your final checkpoint. See the[3-month PSAT study plan](https://acely.com/psat-prep/3-month-psat-study-plan) .


Take your last full test at least a few days before test day so you have time to review it.


## Build a stronger PSAT strategy


### 1) Know the format before test day


Learn the section order, module timing, and how the adaptive format works so the real test feels familiar.


### 2) Practice your timing


Decide ahead of time when you'll move on from a tough question. Use flag-for-review so you can come back to it in the same module.


### 3) Review every question, including the ones you got right


After each practice test, sort misses into content gaps, timing issues, and misreads. Also look at questions you guessed correctly.


### 4) Stay consistent


Short, regular study sessions beat cramming. Even 20 minutes a day adds up.


For section-by-section tactics, read our[PSAT prep strategy guide](https://acely.com/psat-prep/psat-strategy) .


## Create a personal study plan


### Set realistic goals


Use your baseline score to pick a goal score, then break it into smaller weekly targets.


### Schedule dedicated prep time


Put study sessions on your calendar like any other appointment.


### Use practice tests strategically


Cycle through testing, reviewing, and practicing weak skills. Then take another test to check what improved.


Our guide to the[best PSAT prep for 2026](https://acely.com/blog/best-psat-prep-national-merit-guide) compares free and paid options if you want a fuller plan.


## After the PSAT: what to do next


Your PSAT score report shows which skills to work on before the SAT.


- Check your score report in your College Board account when scores are released. Look at section scores and the skills breakdown.
- See where you stand for National Merit if you took the PSAT/NMSQT as a junior. Our[National Merit Scholarship guide](https://acely.com/psat-prep/national-merit-scholarship-guide) explains Selection Index and state cutoffs.
- Use your weakest PSAT skills to prioritize SAT study time. The two tests cover the same skills.
- Take a full-length SAT practice test to set your SAT baseline. You can take one free on Acely with no credit card.[Take a free SAT practice test](https://acely.com/sign-up)
